guide.answer: Medical coding is the process of turning a provider’s visit note into standard codes: ICD-10-CM for diagnoses, CPT and HCPCS for what was done, plus any modifiers. Payers decide what to pay from those codes, so medical coding decides whether a claim is paid in full the first time, is downcoded, denied outright, or flagged in a payer audit years later.
guide.whatP1: Practices code in-house, or outsource medical coding to certified coders. Either way, the real test is the same: does every code match what the note supports, on every chart?
guide.whatP2: Accurate codes, backed by the note, each time.
guide.incIntro: Whoever codes your charts, in-house or a medical coding company, these are the pieces to expect. If one is missing, money leaks.
guide.whyTail: That cost is rarely one big coding error. It’s small, repeatable misses: a missed modifier, an E/M level the note can’t support, vague codes.
guide.whyP2: Because coding misses repeat, fixing the cause is worth more than fixing the claim. That’s why every coding engagement ends each month with provider feedback on the patterns behind your code denials.

guide.answer: Charge entry is the step in medical billing where every service from a visit becomes a line on the claim: the CPT or HCPCS codes, units, modifiers, provider and date. guide.whyP2: Because charge misses repeat, fixing the cause is worth more than fixing the claim. That’s why every charge entry engagement ends each month with missed charges by provider and the fix behind each.

guide.answer: Denial management is the work of getting denied claims paid and stopping the same denials from coming back. It means reading each payer’s reason code, correcting or appealing the claim before the deadline, and tracing every denial to its root cause. Done well, it turns a denial from lost revenue into a late payment, and then into a denial that never happens.

guide.answer: Payment posting is the step in medical billing where each payer’s payment is applied to the claim lines it covers, from an ERA or paper EOB, and balanced to the bank deposit. peer-to-peer-review.description: Peer-to-peer review support: we book the call inside the payer’s window, build the clinical case, brief your physician and file the appeal if it’s upheld.
peer-to-peer-review.platformsCopy: No new software for your staff to learn. Our appeals specialists work inside your EHR to pull chart evidence, track each case in your PM system and payer portal, and we map access with you before anything changes.
peer-to-peer-review.specHeading: Peer-to-peer review support, from people who know specialty payers.
peer-to-peer-review.midBody: Send us a month of denials; we’ll flag every one worth a peer-to-peer call. Free, no contract.
